mainTopic: The order of inheritance between the אב, the בת, and the brothers; why only the father's side counts as משפחה; and the story of יהונתן, the grandson of משה.
overview: The גמרא first defends the reading of ״והעברתם״ that puts a בת ahead of the אב. It then asks each of the two derivations what it does with the other verse. ״שארו״ teaches that a husband inherits his wife, and ״והעברתם״ teaches רבי's rule that only a daughter moves land from one שבט to another. Next the גמרא asks how we know ״שארו״ means the father. רבא answers that only the father's side is called משפחה. A פסוק in שופטים seems to call a לוי ״ממשפחת יהודה״ through his mother. The גמרא explains that this man, יהונתן the grandson of משה, is linked to יהודה and to king מנשה because he worshipped idols like מנשה. From this come teachings that the corrupt are linked to the corrupt, and that a person should marry into a good family. The amud ends with the debate over whether פנחס also descended from יתרו.

steps.title: Maybe the father comes before even a daughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the inheritance never passes away from the אב, even when there is a בת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe you never pass an inheritance away from the father, even when there is a daughter!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the order of inheritance it just learned. Maybe the father inherits before a daughter too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier reading was that ״והעברתם״ means we move the inheritance away from the אב only for a בת, while the father still beats the brothers. The challenge suggests the opposite: the father might beat the daughter as well.

keyTerms.meaning: passes an inheritance on, away from someone

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתָּה מַעֲבִיר נַחֲלָה מִן הָאָב
phrases.english: But you do not pass an inheritance away from the father
phrases.notes: The father here is the father of the person who died.

phrases.english: even where there is a daughter!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אַתָּה מַעֲבִיר נַחֲלָה מִן הָאָב אֲפִילּוּ בִּמְקוֹם בַּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of ״והעברתם״ given just before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a בת comes before the אב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse could be read so that the father beats everyone, including a daughter.

steps.title: The word 'pass' would be unnecessary
steps.stepSummary: If the father came before the daughter, the Torah would not have needed to write ״והעברתם״.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the Torah would not have written 'and you shall pass'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from the wording of the פסוק itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A daughter beats the brothers simply because she is a closer relative, so no special word is needed for that. The word 'pass' tells us the inheritance is moved away from someone who would otherwise get it, and that someone is the אב. So the בת comes before the father.

keyTerms.meaning: the Merciful One, meaning the Torah

phrases.english: If so,
the Merciful One would not write: 'And you shall pass'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The extra word in the פסוק proves the point
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The father might come before even a daughter.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word ״והעברתם״ shows that the בת comes before the אב.
steps.whatToRemember: A בת inherits before the אב. We learn this from the word ״והעברתם״.

steps.title: What does the 'pass' side do with 'his kinsman'?
steps.stepSummary: The person who learns that the father comes before the brothers from ״והעברתם״ must explain why the Torah wrote ״שארו״.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who learns it from 'and you shall pass', what does he do with the word 'his kinsman'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the two derivations it mentioned earlier. It asks the first side what the other verse teaches him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two opinions learn the same rule, that the father beats the brothers, from two different words. Each word in the Torah must teach something. So the side using ״והעברתם״ needs a separate purpose for ״שארו״.

keyTerms.meaning: according to the one who learns it from
what does he do with it?

phrases.english: And according to the one who derives it from 'and you shall pass,'
what does he do with this word 'his kinsman'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּנָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִ״וְהַעֲבַרְתֶּם״, הַאי ״שְׁאֵרוֹ״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defending ״והעברתם״ to comparing the two derivations.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What ״שארו״ teaches according to the side that uses ״והעברתם״.

steps.title: 'His kinsman' teaches that a husband inherits his wife
steps.stepSummary: According to a ברייתא, ״שארו״ means a man's wife. It teaches that a husband inherits from his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what a ברייתא teaches: 'his kinsman' means his wife, which teaches that a husband inherits from his wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this side uses ״שארו״ for a completely different law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For this side, ״שארו״ is not about the father at all. It refers to the wife and teaches that a husband inherits from her. So neither word is wasted.

keyTerms.meaning: a husband inherits from his wife

phrases.english: He requires it for that which is taught in a ברייתא:
'His kinsman' — this is his wife,
which teaches that a husband inherits from his wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״שארו״ is used to teach that a husband inherits from his wife.

steps.title: What does the 'kinsman' side do with 'pass'?
steps.stepSummary: Now the question goes the other way. The side that uses ״שארו״ for the father must explain why the Torah wrote ״והעברתם״.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who learns it from 'his kinsman', what does he do with 'and you shall pass'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question of the second side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This side learns that the father beats the brothers from ״שארו״. So he needs another job for the word ״והעברתם״.

phrases.english: And according to the one who derives it from 'his kinsman,'
what does he do with this word 'and you shall pass'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּנָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִ״שְּׁאֵרוֹ״, הַאי ״וְהַעֲבַרְתֶּם״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the same question as step 3, but of the opposite side.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What ״והעברתם״ teaches according to the side that uses ״שארו״.

steps.title: 'Pass' teaches that only a daughter moves land between tribes
steps.stepSummary: רבי points out that the Torah uses 'giving' for every other heir and 'passing' only for a daughter. Only she can move land from one שבט to another.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what רבי taught. For all the other heirs the Torah says 'giving', but here it says 'passing'. This is because only a daughter moves an inheritance from tribe to tribe, since her son and her husband inherit from her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this side uses ״והעברתם״ for רבי's teaching about tribes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The change from 'giving' to 'passing' hints that land can leave a שבט through a daughter. Her son and her husband may belong to a different tribe, and they inherit from her. So the land passes over to their tribe.
steps.whatToRemember: Each word has its own job. ״שארו״ teaches that a husband inherits his wife. ״והעברתם״ teaches that land moves between tribes only through a בת.

phrases.english: He requires it for that which is taught in a ברייתא —
רבי says: With all of them, the word 'giving' is said,
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means all the other relatives listed in the inheritance verses.

phrases.english: and here, the word 'passing' is said;

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין לְךָ שֶׁמַּעֲבִיר נַחֲלָה מִשֵּׁבֶט לְשֵׁבֶט אֶלָּא בַּת,
phrases.english: for you have no one who passes an inheritance from tribe to tribe except a daughter,
since her son and her husband inherit from her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״והעברתם״ is used for רבי's teaching that only a בת moves land from one שבט to another.

steps.title: How do we know 'his kinsman' means the father?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to ״שארו״ and asks what shows that it refers to the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that 'his kinsman' means the father?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the meaning of ״שארו״. It asks for the source that this word means the father, and the next line gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The side that uses ״שארו״ assumes the word means the אב. The גמרא now asks what that assumption is based on.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that 'his kinsman' — this is the father?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to examine the ״שארו״ derivation itself.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that ״שארו״ means the father.

steps.title: The verse calls a relative 'your father's kinswoman'
steps.stepSummary: The proof is the פסוק ״שאר אביך היא״, where the word שאר is tied to the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'She is your father's kinswoman.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source: the word שאר appears next to 'father' in another פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father's sister is called ״שאר אביך״, the father's close relative. Since שאר is linked to the father there, we read ״שארו״ in the inheritance verses as the father too.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'She is your father's kinswoman.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק ״שאר אביך היא״ links the word שאר to the father.

steps.title: But 'kinswoman' is also used for the mother
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: another פסוק says ״שאר אמך היא״, so maybe ״שארו״ means the mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead that 'his kinsman' means the mother, as it is written: 'For she is your mother's kinswoman'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof it just gave. The same word is used for the mother right next to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on the word שאר appearing with 'father'. But the very next פסוק uses שאר with 'mother'. So the proof does not decide between father and mother. The next step, from רבא, answers this.

phrases.english: Say instead: 'His kinsman' — this is the mother,
as it is written: 'For she is your mother's kinswoman'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof given in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof that ״שארו״ means the father
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word, שאר, is used for the mother in the next פסוק, so the proof is not decisive.

steps.title: Only the father's side is called 'family'
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers the challenge from Step 9. The inheritance פסוק says ״ממשפחתו״, 'from his family,' and the Torah calls only the father's side 'family.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The פסוק says 'from his family, and he shall inherit it.' The father's family is called 'family.' The mother's family is not called 'family,' as it says: 'by their families, by their fathers' houses.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question of Step 9, which asked whether ״שארו״ could mean the mother. He brings a different word from the inheritance פסוק to show that inheritance goes through the father's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the word שאר alone could point to either parent, the inheritance פסוק also says ״ממשפחתו״. The phrase ״למשפחתם לבית אבתם״ shows that 'family' means the father's house, so a mother's relatives are not the 'family' that inherits.

keyTerms.meaning: family; here it means the relatives on the father's side

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the rule that relatives through the mother do not inherit one another as 'family.'

phrases.english: Rava said: the verse says:
"of his family, and he shall inherit it";
the father's family is called "family,"
the mother's family is not called "family" –
as it is written: "by their families, by their fathers' houses."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 9, which said ״שארו״ might mean the mother.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings another word in the inheritance פסוק that settles which side is meant.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״שארו״ could refer to the mother, because of ״שאר אמך היא״.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״ממשפחתו״ limits inheritance to the father's family, since only the father's side is called משפחה.

steps.title: A young man who was a Levite but 'of the family of Judah'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא with a פסוק in שופטים. A young man is called both a לוי and ״ממשפחת יהודה״. This seems to mean his father was from לוי and his mother from יהודה, so the mother's side is called 'family.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Is a mother's family really not called 'family'? It is written: 'There was a young man from בית לחם in יהודה, of the family of יהודה, and he was a לוי.' That itself is hard to understand. 'He was a לוי' means he came from לוי, and 'of the family of יהודה' means he came from יהודה! It must be that his father was from לוי and his mother from יהודה, and still the פסוק says 'of the family of יהודה'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's claim that the mother's side is never called 'family.' It brings a פסוק that seems to call a man's mother's tribe his 'family.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק looks like it contradicts itself, because one man cannot come from two tribes. The only smooth reading is that his father was a לוי and his mother was from יהודה. If so, the Torah calls the mother's tribe his משפחה, which goes against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: this itself is difficult; the פסוק seems to contradict itself
is it not rather that...? Used to push toward one conclusion

phrases.english: And is the mother's family not called "family"?!
But it is written:
"And there was a young man from Bethlehem in Judah

phrases.aramaic: מִמִּשְׁפַּחַת יְהוּדָה, וְהוּא לֵוִי, וְהוּא גָר שָׁם״ –
phrases.english: of the family of Judah, and he was a Levite, and he lived there" –
this itself is difficult;
you said "he was a Levite" – apparently he comes from Levi,
"of the family of Judah" – apparently he comes from Judah!

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו דַּאֲבוּהּ מִלֵּוִי, וְאִימֵּיהּ מִיהוּדָה?
phrases.english: Is it not rather that his father was from Levi, and his mother from Judah?
And yet it says "of the family of Judah"!

steps.triggerLanguage: ומשפחת אם אינה קרויה משפחה?! והא כתיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's claim in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that the mother's family is not called משפחה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק calls a לוי ״ממשפחת יהודה״. The only way to make sense of that is through his mother, so a mother's tribe is called 'family.'

steps.title: 'Levi' was just his name
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רב חנן answers that the man was not from שבט לוי at all. He was from יהודה, and 'לוי' was his personal name.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר רב חנן said: No. It means a man whose name was לוי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר רב חנן gets rid of the contradiction. He reads ״והוא לוי״ as the man's name, not his tribe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'לוי' is a name, the man was simply from יהודה through his father. Nothing in the פסוק then calls the mother's tribe 'family,' and רבא's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: a man whose name was לוי

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'לוי' here as the tribe. רבא בר רב חנן's whole answer is that it is only the man's first name.

phrases.english: Rava bar Rav Ḥanan said:
No; it means a man whose name was Levi.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבא בר רב חנן: לא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets a word in the פסוק as a name rather than a tribe.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״והוא לוי״ means he was from שבט לוי, so ״ממשפחת יהודה״ must be his mother's side.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was from יהודה through his father, and לוי was just his name.

steps.title: Why was Micah so happy to have 'the Levite'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. מיכה rejoiced that he had 'the לוי' as a כהן, which only makes sense if the man really was from שבט לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, how do we understand what מיכה said: 'Now I know that ה׳ will do good to me, because I have the לוי as a כהן'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבא בר רב חנן's answer from a later פסוק in the same story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מיכה's joy seems tied to having a real member of שבט לוי serve as his כהן. If 'לוי' were only a name, it is hard to see why that would make him so glad.

keyTerms.meaning: is that why he said...? Asking how a quote fits
the man in שופטים who set up an idol and hired this young man

phrases.english: If so, is that what Micah said:
"Now I know that the Lord will do good to me,
for I have the Levite as a priest"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא בר רב חנן's reading that 'לוי' was only a name.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מיכה's words suggest the man's being a לוי meant something real, which fits only if he was from שבט לוי.

steps.title: Micah saw the name as a good sign
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רב חנן answers that מיכה was simply happy that a man named לוי happened to come his way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. He was happy because a man named לוי happened to come to him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר רב חנן defends his reading. מיכה's joy was about the lucky name, not about the man's tribe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name alone was enough for מיכה to feel things were going well. So his words do not prove that the man came from שבט לוי.

keyTerms.meaning: it happened to him; it came his way by chance

phrases.english: Yes, because there happened to come to him
a man whose name was Levi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the quoted words in a way that fits the name reading.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מיכה rejoiced because the man was truly from שבט לוי.
steps.terutzMaskana: מיכה rejoiced at the lucky chance of getting a man named לוי.

steps.title: But his name was Jonathan
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again. Another פסוק says this man's name was יהונתן בן גרשם בן מנשה, so how could his name be לוי?
steps.simpleTranslation: Was his name really לוי? Wasn't his name יהונתן? As it says: 'And יהונתן son of גרשם son of מנשה, he and his sons were כהנים for שבט דן.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the claim that 'לוי' was the man's name. It brings a פסוק that gives his name as יהונתן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק tells us his actual name was יהונתן, then reading 'לוי' as a name looks wrong. That would bring back the reading that he was from שבט לוי.

keyTerms.meaning: is it really so that...? A doubtful question

phrases.english: And was his name Levi?!
But wasn't Jonathan his name, as it is stated:
"And Jonathan son of Gershom son of Manasseh,

phrases.aramaic: הוּא וּבָנָיו הָיוּ כֹהֲנִים לְשֵׁבֶט הַדָּנִי״!
phrases.english: he and his sons were priests to the tribe of the Danites"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וכי לוי שמו?! והלא יהונתן שמו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new challenge to the name reading that Step 14 defended.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'לוי' was the man's personal name.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק gives his name as יהונתן, so 'לוי' cannot be his name.

steps.title: Your reading has the same problem: he was Moses' grandson
steps.stepSummary: The reply turns the question around. The same פסוק calls him 'בן מנשה,' yet גרשם was the son of משה. So that פסוק can't be read literally on anyone's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: (He said to him: And according to your reasoning,) was he really the son of מנשה? Wasn't he the son of משה? As it is written: 'The sons of משה: גרשום and אליעזר'!
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of answering directly, the reply shows that the questioner's own פסוק can't be taken literally either. The גמרא is setting up an explanation of how this פסוק uses names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says גרשם was 'בן מנשה,' but דברי הימים says גרשם was the son of משה. So the family names in this story cannot all be read literally. The next step uses this to explain both 'בן מנשה' and 'ממשפחת יהודה' as descriptions of his deeds. That leaves him a real לוי, the grandson of משה.

keyTerms.meaning: and according to your reasoning; turns a question back on the asker

phrases.english: (He said to him: And according to your reasoning,)
phrases.notes: The words in round brackets are in the standard printed גמרא, but some versions leave them out. Either way, the line goes on to raise the same problem.

phrases.english: is he really the son of Manasseh?!
But isn't he the son of Moses,
as it is written: "The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה: וליטעמיך, וכי בן מנשה הוא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to Step 15 by showing that the same פסוק has a problem on the questioner's view too.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counter-challenge (וליטעמיך) showing the proof פסוק cannot be read literally.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק in שופטים gives his real name as יהונתן, so 'לוי' cannot be his name.
steps.terutzMaskana: That פסוק also says 'בן מנשה' when he was really a descendant of משה, so its family names are not literal. This sets up the figurative reading in step 17.

steps.title: He acted like מנשה, so the פסוק links him to מנשה and to יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The reply ends by explaining both nicknames. יהונתן is called 'בן מנשה' because he behaved like the wicked king מנשה. He is called 'ממשפחת יהודה' because that same מנשה came from יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, since he acted the way מנשה acted, the פסוק linked him to מנשה. Here too: since he acted like מנשה, who came from יהודה, the פסוק linked him to יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer from Step 16. It explains why the פסוק calls this man 'בן מנשה' and also 'from the family of יהודה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees he was really the grandson of משה, so 'בן מנשה' cannot mean his real father. It describes his behavior: he served idols like king מנשה. In the same way, 'ממשפחת יהודה' does not describe his tribe. It links him to מנשה's tribe, so he can still be a real לוי.

keyTerms.meaning: The deeds of מנשה, meaning idol worship
The פסוק hung him on, meaning it linked or attached him to

steps.confusionAlert: This מנשה is the wicked king of יהודה, not מנשה the son of יוסף. That is why being linked to him also links the man to יהודה.

phrases.english: Rather, since he acted the way מנשה acted,
phrases.notes: This is king מנשה of יהודה, who was known for serving idols.

phrases.english: the verse linked him to מנשה;
here too,
since he acted the way מנשה acted,
and מנשה came from יהודה,
the verse linked him to יהודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reply that began in Step 16 by giving the figurative reading. This finally answers Step 11's challenge to רבא: 'ממשפחת יהודה' describes his deeds, not his mother's tribe.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Figurative reading of the פסוק: a person is linked by his deeds, not by family
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'בן מנשה' and 'ממשפחת יהודה' describe his real family, so he was not a לוי
steps.terutzMaskana: Both phrases describe his behavior. He was a real לוי, the grandson of משה, who acted like the idol-worshipping king מנשה of יהודה.

steps.title: The corrupt are linked to the corrupt
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי שמעון בן יוחי, learns a general idea from this פסוק. Scripture attaches a corrupt person to someone else who was corrupt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: From here we learn that corruption is linked to the corrupt.
steps.whatsHappening: Building on the last step, the גמרא brings a general principle. The פסוק ties a bad person to an earlier bad person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהונתן had no family tie to מנשה or יהודה. The פסוק linked him to them only because of shared wrongdoing. רבי שמעון בן יוחי turns this into a rule about how Scripture describes people.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי:
phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי:
From here we learn that we attach
the corruption to the corrupt one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general principle from the reading in Step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Scripture attaches a corrupt person's identity to another corrupt person, as יהונתן was attached to מנשה.

steps.title: A different source: אדוניה is linked to אבשלום
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא learns the same principle from a different פסוק. אדוניה is described as if he had the same mother as אבשלום, even though their mothers were different. This is because both rebelled against the kingdom.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: we learn it from here: 'He was also very handsome, and she bore him after אבשלום.' But אדוניה was the son of חגית, and אבשלום was the son of מעכה! Rather, since he acted like אבשלום, who rebelled against the kingdom, the פסוק linked him to אבשלום. Here too, since he acted like מנשה, the פסוק linked him to מנשה.
steps.whatsHappening: A second Sage brings a different source for the same idea. He shows a פסוק that links two brothers with different mothers because they did the same bad thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'she bore him after אבשלום', which sounds like they shared a mother, yet they did not. So the link must be about behavior: both tried to take the throne from דוד. He then applies this back to יהונתן and מנשה.

keyTerms.meaning: From here, meaning from this other פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: Scripture can call someone the 'son' or 'brother' of a person he is not related to, because he copied that person's bad deeds.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא אָמַר, מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: we learn it from here:
"And he was also very handsome,"
phrases.notes: מלכים א 1:6, talking about אדוניה son of דוד.

phrases.english: "and she bore him after אבשלום"
phrases.notes: This sounds as if one mother gave birth to both of them.

phrases.english: But wasn't אדוניה the son of חגית,
and אבשלום the son of מעכה!
Rather, since he acted the way אבשלום acted,
who rebelled against the kingdom,
the verse linked him to אבשלום.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי, מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁעָשָׂה מַעֲשֵׂה מְנַשֶּׁה –
phrases.english: Here too, since he acted the way מנשה acted,
the verse linked him to מנשה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא אָמַר, מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different פסוק as the source for the principle in Step 18.
steps.raayaObject: The principle that Scripture links a corrupt person to an earlier corrupt person
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים א 1:6: אדוניה is described as born 'after אבשלום' as though from the same mother, because both rebelled against the kingdom

steps.title: Always attach yourself to good people
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that a person should marry into a good family. משה married the daughter of יתרו, an idol priest, and יהונתן, an idol priest, descended from him. אהרן married the daughter of עמינדב, and פנחס descended from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: A person should always attach himself to good people. For משה married the daughter of יתרו, and יהונתן came from him. אהרן married the daughter of עמינדב, and פנחס came from him.
steps.whatsHappening: Since we have been talking about יהונתן the grandson of משה, the גמרא brings a related teaching. Who you marry affects what kind of children come from you.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both brothers were great, yet their descendants were very different. רבי אלעזר explains the difference through their wives' families. יתרו's past idol worship showed up in יהונתן, while עמינדב's fine family showed up in פנחס.

keyTerms.meaning: Came out from him, descended from him

phrases.english: רבי אלעזר said:
A person should always attach himself to good people,
for משה, who married the daughter of יתרו,
יהונתן came from him;
אהרן, who married the daughter of עמינדב,
פנחס came from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new related teaching, sparked by the discussion of יהונתן the grandson of משה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Marry into good families, because the wife's family shapes the descendants: יתרו led to יהונתן, and עמינדב led to פנחס.

steps.title: Didn't פנחס also come from יתרו?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר's contrast. פנחס's mother was from 'the daughters of פוטיאל', and פוטיאל seems to be a name for יתרו, who fattened calves for idols. If so, פנחס also descended from יתרו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And didn't פנחס also come from יתרו? But it is written: 'And אלעזר son of אהרן took for himself one of the daughters of פוטיאל as a wife.' Doesn't this mean he came from יתרו, who fattened calves for idol worship?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי אלעזר's example. It suggests that פנחס also had יתרו in his family, which would ruin the contrast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר's point needs פנחס to have no tie to יתרו. The פסוק about פנחס's mother says she was from 'פוטיאל', and the גמרא reads that name as a hint to יתרו, who 'פיטם' (fattened) calves for idols. Then both brothers' lines would include יתרו.

keyTerms.meaning: The grandfather of פנחס on his mother's side

phrases.english: And didn't פנחס also come from יתרו?
But it is written:
"And אלעזר son of אהרן took for himself
one of the daughters of פוטיאל as a wife";
what, doesn't it mean he came from יתרו,
who fattened calves for idol worship?
phrases.notes: A play on the name: פוטיאל sounds like פיטם, 'fattened'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the example in Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's contrast between משה's descendants (from יתרו) and אהרן's descendants (פנחס)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If פוטיאל is יתרו, then פנחס also descends from יתרו, so יתרו's lineage cannot explain the difference between יהונתן and פנחס.

steps.title: No, פוטיאל refers to יוסף, who fought his desire
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'פוטיאל' may hint at יוסף instead, who struggled against his desire. So פנחס's mother's side comes from יוסף, not necessarily from יתרו.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means he came from יוסף, who fought against his evil inclination.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אלעזר. It reads the name 'פוטיאל' a different way, as a hint to יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name פוטיאל can also be read as 'פטפט', struggled against, which points to יוסף, who fought his desire. With this reading, פנחס's ancestry is linked to a righteous person, so רבי אלעזר's contrast stands.
steps.whatToRemember: פוטיאל can be read two ways: יתרו who fattened calves (פיטם), or יוסף who fought his desire (פטפט). The גמרא uses the second reading to defend רבי אלעזר, but the next step challenges it.

phrases.english: No, it means he came from יוסף,
who struggled against his desire.
phrases.notes: Another play on פוטיאל: here it is read as פטפט, 'struggled'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternate reading of the name פוטיאל
steps.terutzHavaAmina: פוטיאל means יתרו, who fattened calves for idols, so פנחס also descends from יתרו
steps.terutzMaskana: פוטיאל can mean יוסף, who struggled against his desire, so פנחס is not shown to come from יתרו and רבי אלעזר's contrast stands

steps.title: The tribes mocked פנחס for his idol-fattening grandfather
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer that פנחס came only from יוסף. The tribes insulted פנחס as the grandson of someone who fattened calves for idols, which points to יתרו.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't the tribes insult פנחס and say: 'Have you seen this son of פוטי? His mother's father fattened calves for idol worship, and he dares to kill a prince of a tribe of Israel?!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 22. It brings the tribes' insult against פנחס as proof that his mother's father was יתרו, the man who fattened calves for idols.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 tried to read 'פוטיאל' as a hint to יוסף, so that פנחס would not descend from יתרו. But the tribes clearly called his mother's father an idol-calf fattener, and that describes יתרו. So the problem from step 21 comes back: פנחס also descends from יתרו, which weakens רבי אלעזר's contrast between משה and אהרן.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Son of פוטי', a mocking nickname for פנחס
Prince or leader of a tribe (here זמרי)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Him' here is פנחס, not יתרו. The insult is about פנחס's grandfather on his mother's side, and that is exactly the question being argued about.

phrases.english: But didn't the tribes insult him,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is פנחס, after he killed זמרי (במדבר 25).

phrases.english: and say: 'Have you seen this son of פוטי?'
The son whose mother's father fattened
phrases.notes: The word פוטי sounds like פיטם, 'fattened'. That was the point of the mocking name.

phrases.english: calves for idol worship.
Should he kill a prince of a tribe of Israel?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of step 22, which said that פוטיאל refers to יוסף and not to יתרו.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 22 that פנחס's mother's side came from יוסף rather than from יתרו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The tribes called פנחס's maternal grandfather someone who fattened calves for idols, and that matches יתרו. So פנחס does descend from יתרו.
